title: Pack a skate with its spring guard fitted
instruction: Put the skate in the gear bag.
context: A person reaching into a gear bag can cut a hand on the exposed runner of an ice skate. The loose two-piece guard protects the dry runner by capturing its toe and heel under spring tension. Fitting it requires controlling the skew of the skate while extending the guard enough to engage both ends.
setup: On a standard two-arm bench, all long axes parallel to the line between the arms: one dry 610 g adult-size synthetic skate, 272 × 92 × 157 mm with a blunt 243 mm steel runner, lies on its side with the runner facing away from the arms. A loose 31 mm wide polymer dual-spring guard rests on its side on a 29 mm wooden shim, its empty channel facing the runner. It starts closed at 227 mm between its two inner end stops, with 54 mm available travel. An empty teal padded gear bag is open with a 189 × 303 mm internal floor and roughly 65 mm walls. Measured from the midpoint of the arm bases, the runner datum is 414 mm forward and 150 mm left, the guard datum is 475 mm forward and 150 mm left, and the bag is 419 mm forward and 151 mm right. See the README for the guard spring load, dimensions and reset details.
scoring: 1.0 for a released skate completely inside the bag footprint with its runner below the walls and covered by a seated guard at both ends, held for 0.5 s; 0.5 for a released, settled skate with both cups retaining the runner outside the bag; 0.0 otherwise. Bare-runner packing latches 0.0 for the trial. A visible gap of up to 9 mm at either stop and an extension of 13–45 mm above the guard’s fully closed 227 mm spacing count as fitted when the runner is seated in the channel at both ends. See the README for numeric alignment tolerances and how to check fit.
reset_notes: Remove and unclip the skate, let both springs retract the empty guard, and replace the skate, guard and open bag at their marked positions. Clear the bag compartment. The blade is dry and blunt for safe trials.
fidelity: Full-size inert boot and metal runner, real end-stop and channel contacts, 54 mm guided travel, and an equivalent 105 N/m dual-spring return. The ends retain the runner under spring tension. The printed guard uses a guided joint; fixed panels model a propped-open padded bag.
